entertainment.title: Emma Chamberlain Returning to YouTube With Original Series ‘What Are You Waiting For?’ (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The veteran creator is ditching the vlog format for a docuseries concept.
entertainment.body:
One of YouTube ‘s original superstars is planning a major comeback to the platform.

Emma Chamberlain, whose vlogs on the platform propelled her to stardom (she has more than 12 million followers there), is launching a new show on YouTube next year, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

Chamberlain will launch the docuseries What Are You Waiting For? in which she explores some of New York’s most popular lines, and the people waiting in them.

“ What Are You Waiting For? on the surface is about people who voluntarily wait in lines for stuff set in New York City, a phenomenon that I personally don’t understand but seek to understand, and along the way I discover much more about humanity than I ever could have expected,” Chamberlain says. “The experience of making this was unlike anything I have ever done and has profoundly changed me as a person, talking to strangers all day, working with a crew of unbelievably talented people, and making something bigger than I have ever made before, I feel the next chapter of my life coming to fruition, and I am deeply inspired and grateful.”

The show is being produced in partnership with Amplify Pictures, underscoring how content on YouTube is professionalizing and becoming more ambitious. In fact, Chamberlain is debuting the new concept at a YouTube Creator Premieres event in Los Angeles Tuesday evening, with Wesley Wang and Aryna Sabalenka also making appearances.

It’s also a coup for the platform, which has been trying to entice top creators to develop shows and programming primarily for itself at a moment when there are a number of competitors pursuing deals with top talent.

“After deciding to take a hiatus from my podcast, I spent the next few months trying to figure out what I wanted to create next,” Chamberlain says. “The answer wasn’t obvious at first, but I knew for sure that I wanted to make something for YouTube. From entertaining me as a child to allowing me to build a career as an adult, it was a no-brainer that whatever I make next had to go on YouTube.”

“Working with a TV studio to create YouTube content is a full 180 from what I have done in the past, producing everything myself with very little help, but I knew this was crucial,” she added. “I met with Joe Lewis and Amplify Pictures and explained a little idea I had for a docuseries. To my surprise, they loved it and wanted to make it with me.”

entertainment.title: Live Nation’s 17,000 Gather Brisbane Project Is Approved
entertainment.summary: Live Nation, OVG and Plenary will build the arena, which will have an 18,700 capacity in concert mode and which, the team behind it say, should bring more major live events to the city.
entertainment.body:
BRISBANE, Australia – The capital of the Sunshine State, Brisbane, will become a two-arena city when a new 17,000-capacity venue is completed ahead of the 2032 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games.

A years-long wait for approval came to end this week when Gather Brisbane was rubber stamped, a major new live music and entertainment project for the inner-city suburb of Woolloongabba. Related CL Signs With THEBLACKLABEL, Reuniting With Longtime Producer Teddy For 'Full Circle' Moment Jeff Benjamin

Live Nation, OVG and Plenary will build the arena, which will have an 18,700 capacity in concert mode and which, the team behind it say, should bring more major live events to Brisbane.

According to forecasts presented by Live Nation, the arena is expected to welcome more than 1.2 million people each year, support upwards of 1,500 ongoing jobs and generate almost A$844 million ($568 million) annually for the city’s visitor economy.

“Brisbane has the audience and the ambition to welcome more of the world’s biggest tours, but it needs the venues to match,” comments Michael Coppel, chairman of Live Nation Australia and New Zealand. “This arena will help bring more shows to Queensland, strengthen Australia’s appeal as a touring destination and give artists and fans an arena they can be proud of for decades to come.”

Brisbane won the rights to host the Olympics in 2021 when the IOC declared the city as the “preferred candidate,” thanks to its proven track record for organizing international events, with the Commonwealth Games (two, including the Gold Coast), an Expo and the Goodwill Games in its good books.

And critically, the region already had up to 90% of the essential pieces of infrastructure in place — although a cornerstone stadium, bettering the aging Brisbane Cricket Ground (The Gabba) at Woolloongabba, and the Queensland Sport and Athletics Centre at Mount Gravatt, has been both a sore point and a political football.

The creation of a new, world-class arena, one to complement, and outlive, the Brisbane Entertainment Centre, which opened its doors in 1986, was part of the bargain.

"I want to say you have been dealing with everything with grace, with the noise outside," Shum told Johnson, "and teaching me the things that I have only dreamed of to learn, and this has been one of the most beautiful experiences. So, thank you so much."

entertainment.title: Noah Kahan Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nominations Snub: ‘I Was In My Feelings for a Sec’
entertainment.summary: While Kahan did receive one folk nomination, the singer/songwriter was expected to show up across the Big Four categories.
entertainment.body:
Before the 2027 Grammy nominations were announced on Monday morning, Noah Kahan was expected to have a big presence across the Big Four categories with his latest album The Great Divide . But once all the nominees were revealed, Kahan only had a single nomination: best contemporary folk album.

The singer/songwriter became the poster child for countless “snubs & surprises” lists ( Billboard ‘s included ), and the only thing fans heard from Kahan on Monday was this three-word tweet: “Life goes on.”

But he had more to say on Tuesday (Nov. 17), taking to X to thank fans and congratulate his fellow nominees.

“Needed a day to just recalibrate but I want to say THANK YOU so much for the support and love,” he wrote. “I also want to offer a huge congratulations to every nominee. They all deserve it and I am proud to have been considered in the same company!”

Kahan also took the time to reply to some messages on X. One fan wrote to him, “Glad you took the time you needed, there is no alternate universe in which we could be prouder of you or more grateful for your music,” to which Kahan responded: “And that recognition is truly what’s most important to me. I was in my feelings for a sec but nobody is owed anything in this life, and I got a bunch of fans to play songs for! Love you guys so much.”

He also heard from Vermont congresswoman Becca Balint, who posted a video on X in which she said: “Hey, Vermonters. We were robbed. Not a single Noah Kahan nomination in the Grammys .” (Balint corrected her error in the video text, adding “Couldn’t think straight. He did get one.”) “It’s just not right. Not right.” Kahan responded to the Democratic U.S. representative, “As long as you keep winning I’ll be happy! Thank you so much and thanks for what you do for our state.”

Before Monday, Kahan had two Grammy nominations under his belt, including for best new artist in 2024.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs is on pace to break the NFL record for yards from scrimmage in a season
sports.summary: The current record belongs to Chris Johnson, who had 2,509 yards for the Titans in 2009.
sports.body:
Through nine games this season, Gibbs has an NFL-high 1,000 rushing yards. Gibbs also has 384 receiving yards. That total of 1,384 yards from scrimmage leads the league, and with an average of 153.8 yards per game, Gibbs is on pace total 2,614 yards from scrimmage over a 17-game season.

That would break the NFL record, held by Chris Johnson of the Titans, who totaled 2,509 yards from scrimmage (2,006 rushing yards and 503 receiving yards) in 2009.

Gibbs has touched the ball an NFL-high 240 times this season, combining 199 carries and 41 catches. With that kind of workload, the biggest concern for the Lions will be whether he can stay healthy for 17 regular-season games and, the Lions hope, some playoff games after that.

But given how well Gibbs is playing, it would be hard for Dan Campbell and the Lions’ coaching staff to reduce his workload. He’s having a special season. He’s halfway to one of the greatest seasons any running back has ever had.

On average, 27.13 million watched the 46-40 barnburner, which ultimately underscored the fact that: (1) the 49ers are elite; and (2) the old “Doomsday Defense” nickname has a much different meaning now.

The performance of the game reconfirms the fact that 4:25 p.m. ET has become the most valuable weekly window. It currently rotates between CBS and FOX, with multiple simultaneous games per year.

It’s hard not to imagine the NFL considering breaking that window away from the standard Sunday afternoon packages and selling it to one network. Given the size of the audiences, it would be the most lucrative package the NFL could offer.

sports.title: Officials who were bumped by reconfigured Week 10 schedule won't lose pay
sports.summary: The four officials who worked two games in Week 10 got paid accordingly.
sports.body:
NFL Referees Association executive director Scott Green tells PFT that the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the NFL and the NFLRA “requires that all active officials including anybody out with an injury are guaranteed 16 games of pay during the regular season regardless if they work all 16 games.”

Of course, it’s possible that the NFL will reconfigure upcoming assignments to balance out the total assignments, putting an official who was supposed to work a given weekend on a bye while assigning an official to work when the official was supposed to be off. (That’s not something Green said; it’s our own assessment of how the imbalance can be rectified.)

Hopefully, that won’t happen. Those who were supposed to work but didn’t should get credit for the game, since they were prepared to show up and do the job. And those who worked when they weren’t supposed to shouldn’t lose the opportunity to work their otherwise normal schedule — unless they choose that.

And the four who worked two games in one day should absolutely get some sort of a bonus. As Green said, "[T]hat’s pretty remarkable as you are generally pretty wiped out both mentally and physically after working a game.”

The fact that Don Willard, Terry Killens, Jabir Walker, and Justin Larrew went above and beyond the call makes a reward not just appropriate but necessary.

sports.title: At NC State, Philip Rivers will be one of the lowest-paid Power 4 coaches
sports.summary: Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers earned $244 million during his playing career.
sports.body:
Via Kennington Smith III of Front Office Sports , Rivers will make $3.25 million in his first year as the head coach at NC State.

That puts him among the lowest-paid Power 4 coaches whose compensation is publicly known, and in the same range as Cincinnati’s Scott Satterfield ($3.8 million), Oklahoma State’s Eric Morris ($3.8 million), West Virginia’s Rich Rodriguez ($3.6 million), and Iowa State’s Jimmy Rogers ($3 million).

The less Rivers takes, the more that is available for players. And Rivers is confident that the investment will be made.

“It’s been very clear in our talks that they’re committed to doing everything that they can do to help the football program,” Rivers said at his introductory press conference, via Smith. “This thing is still about people. Having belief and confidence in people. So for me, we don’t need to pull out spreadsheets and go through every penny; but it’s a belief that we’re going to do everything we can to get North Carolina State to the top.”

Rivers also realizes that his lack of experience points to a lower entry-level rate, beyond the question of leaving money around for his staff and his players.

“You can’t negate the experience I’ve had in 25 years, but the truth is I am a first-time head coach in Power 4 football,” Rivers said. “So I think in some ways that makes sense in that reflection from a contract standpoint, but those other things are true too.”

If it works, he’ll surely get more from NC State. And doors will open elsewhere. Earlier this year, Rivers was interviewed for the head-coaching vacancy with the Bills. If Rivers turns the Wolfpack into a contender, other NFL teams inevitably will come calling.

And in that situation, in those situations, I feel like I did. And so, that’s the frustrating part that lingers.”

Williams had thrown four total interceptions in the 11 games before the Bucs game, dating to Nov. 28, 2025. He had never thrown more than two in a game.

“He’s playing fast right now,” Johnson said. “He’s got a great approach. He’s doing a good job downloading the game plan. We don’t feel like we’re hindered in any way as a coaching staff from the schematics of what we’re able to put in, the details, the alerts. He’s just able to digest a lot more. He’s seeing coverage really well with where his eyes should be tied into his feet also. So, we’re really encouraged with where he’s at. We’ve just got to continue to push that envelope and see how far it will take us.”

During his break, Williams’ close friend, Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, won the National League MVP award. Williams’ odds to win NFL MVP are +3500.

Williams was asked whether Chicago is big enough to handle two MVPs.

sports.title: Dan Campbell won't wallow in "what ifs" arising from injuries
sports.summary: The Lions have, in recent weeks, lost both linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) to significant injuries.
sports.body:
“I think there’s times where, if you’re not careful, you lay in bed at night and you start thinking about all the ‘what ifs,’” Campbell told reporters on Tuesday. “And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of shit. And I’m not gonna do it, man. We’re not doing it.

“I refuse to look at it that way. Does it sting? Yeah, it sure did in the moment. It’s time to move on. We have to.

“And what has happened with Jack Campbell and with Hutch now will not be in vain. We can’t allow it to. They got us to this point. And so what are we gonna do about it, man? Are we just gonna let it go to waste, or are we gonna do something and pick up the slack?”

It’s the right attitude. Injuries happen. Sometimes, they happen to great players. (The more great players a team has, the greater the chances that one of them will be injured.)

The only approach is to tap the next man up on the shoulder, expect him to do his job to the best of his ability, not allow it to become a “woe is us” situation, and keep going.

That becomes easier, of course, if a team has quality depth. Which is why some teams that are top heavy with highly-paid stars find themselves in a pinch when those stars aren’t available to play.

sports.title: ESPN chief: Media coverage of Joe Buck, Troy Aikman dustup is "disappointing"
sports.summary: The Joe Buck vs.
sports.body:
“Joe and Troy have done a great job for us on Monday Night Football .” ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro said Tuesday at the SBJ Media Innovators conference, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing . “When I say ‘us,’ they’ve done a great job for ESPN, they’ve done a great job for the league, they’ve done a great job for the game, and most importantly, they’ve done a great job for fans.

“Are we happy about the media coverage recently? Of course not. It’s been disappointing . But these guys are professionals, and they’re delivering every week. If you watched it last night, another super high-quality production and telecast, and I’d fully expect that to continue that through the season and through the Super Bowl.”

At some level, they shouldn’t be disappointed. Any attention is, at some level, good attention. While it’s unlikely that anyone is tuning in for a Monday night game solely to witness the interactions of Buck and Aikman, it adds a little extra something to the overall buzz arising from the broadcast.

The deeper question is who Pitaro and the other big shots at ESPN are “disappointed” with. The situation didn’t come to light because everyone involved decided to keep the dirty laundry in house. People started talking privately. Aikman has said plenty publicly that confirms the situation and otherwise stirs the pot.

ESPN has no cause to be disappointed with those who did their jobs by pulling the threads of a genuinely interesting, uncontived, and in many ways unprecedented story. If the folks who write the checks should be miffed at anyone, it should be at the recipients of those checks who decided not to hold their own tongues in check regarding an obviously sensitive situation.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills roster moves: DB Te’Cory Couch signed to practice squad
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills announced a series of roster moves as they begin preparations to host the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium for Week 11. Buffalo has signed defensive back Te’Cory Couch to the practice squad, bringing him back to One Bills Drive after being released ahead of last weekend’s game an
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills announced a series of roster moves as they begin preparations to host the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium for Week 11. Buffalo has signed defensive back Te’Cory Couch to the practice squad, bringing him back to One Bills Drive after being released ahead of last weekend’s game and once he cleared waivers Monday afternoon. The 27-year-old defender out of the University of Miami has played in four games for Buffalo this season. In those games, Couch has made eight tackles (6 solo), showcasing a knack for limiting big plays after the catch with solid tackling. Couch joined the Bills in 2024, entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent. To make room for Couch, Buffalo once again parted ways with veteran offensive guard Nick Broeker, who has been re-added to the team’s practice squad several times already this season. Broeker has yet to appear in a regular-season game for the Bills, though he has previously played in 12 games (2023 and 2024 seasons) for the Denver Broncos. Broeker was originally drafted by Buffalo in Round 7 (230th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. The Bills also announced that rookie offensive guard Ar’maj Reed-Adams has been placed on Injured Reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games. With Reed-Adams heading to IR, that opens up a spot on Buffalo’s 53-man roster. A potential candidate to take over that roster opening is veteran wide receiver Tyrell Shavers, whose return-to-practice window was recently opened as the next step toward a return to the field following a devastating knee injury against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the Bills’ 2025 NFL playoff run.

sports.title: The NFL officials who pulled double duty got double pay (as they should)
sports.summary: Some things go without saying.
sports.body:
Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports , the four officials who ended up officiating two games on Sunday (Don Willard, Terry Killens, Jabir Walker, and Justin Larrew) will get paid for working two games .

Why wouldn’t they? Getting twice the pay for twice the work should be a given. The real question is whether they should have gotten even more.

Folks who work overtime usually get time-and-a-half pay. In some instances, going above and beyond the call of duty results in double pay.

Here’s the real question — did the officials who were supposed to work one game in Week 10 but didn’t get still get their pay? Or do officials only get paid for the games they actually officiate, even if/when the NFL seemingly overreacts, reshuffles the deck, and cancels an official’s assignment that the official was otherwise ready and willing to fulfill?

It still seems that the NFL overreacted to the situation , turning the officiating assignments upside down in lieu of deciding to do whatever needed to be done to get the officials to their assigned game so that the existing crews wouldn’t be disrupted.

sports.title: For the Seahawks this year, Drew Lock's numbers blow Sam Darnold's away
sports.summary: When Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Sam Darnold will start in Week 12 against the 49ers, assuming he is medically cleared, it was no surprise: The Seahawks signed Darnold to a three-year, $100 million contract last year and won the Super Bowl with Darnold at the helm.
sports.body:
But Drew Lock has made it reasonable to question whether Darnold should get benched.

That’s because Lock has played three full games, and most of a fourth, while Darnold has missed time with injuries this season. And Lock hasn’t just been better than Darnold. Lock has been so much better that there’s no comparison between the two.

The Seahawks are 4-0 in the games when Lock was their primary quarterback. They’re 2-4 in the games with Darnold as the primary quarterback.

Of the 37 NFL quarterbacks who have thrown at least 90 passes this season, Lock ranks first with a passer rating of 125.6. Darnold ranks 31st with a passer rating of 79.5.

Lock has still not thrown an interception this season. Darnold has thrown nine.

Lock has completed 73.1 percent of his passes. Darnold has completed 60.2 percent.

Lock is averaging 9.0 yards per pass. Darnold is averaging 7.0 yards per pass.

Lock has been sacked on 5.1 percent of his dropbacks. Darnold has been sacked on 7.5 percent of his dropbacks.

sports.title: Mike LaFleur "really encouraged" by Carson Beck's first start
sports.summary: Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck had a rough go of it in his first start, falling 34-6 to the Rams.
sports.body:
Beck’s opportunities were limited, as the Cardinals possessed the ball for just 17:37 to the Rams’ 42:23. He finished the contest 11-of-18 for 108 yards with two interceptions — though one of them went right off his receiver’s hands and into the arms of a defender.

In his Monday press conference, head coach Mike LaFleur said he’s encouraged by what he saw from the young QB.

“Was he doing his job? Was he getting in and out of the huddle? I thought he used the cadence really well, got that first free play on that third and seven,” LaFleur said, via transcript from the team. “Actually, I chickened out a little bit because we talked about using cadence all week when we were kind of in those disadvantaged situations. The first drive, I kind of wanted to chill out and make sure that we weren’t going from third-and-seven to third-and-12, and he stuck with it. He stuck with the cadence there, got the free play, and I thought [he] delivered an excellent ball to our receiver. I know our receiver can make that play.

“When you just look at his element and what he had to do, like I said yesterday, he did everything we asked him to do, and I am really encouraged by it.”

LaFleur went on to say it was a “sharp” debut from Beck, though he also noted that some moments may have been a bit overwhelming for the rookie QB.

“I think we all probably could notice that, right? I mean, you guys could see with your eyes,” LaFleur said. “As I was talking to you guys right after the game, you guys saw it, and then you confirmed it probably with some tape today or whatever you guys were watching. That wasn’t shocking at all. It’s just like I’ve kind of said with him, you can meet all you want, and you can watch all the film, [but] he keeps it very simple. At least that’s what it comes across as.

“It’s just going to be getting as many reps as he can. That’s what stinks about yesterday [was] only having 34 reps and trying to get a little bit of a run game going, which we obviously didn’t. Not a huge sample size as of yesterday, but hey, have another one this week, and we’ll take it from there.”

sports.title: Packers players will get their mandatory four days off after Week 12 game
sports.summary: The Packers have a bye in Week 11.
sports.body:
Coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Monday that, after discussions with the NFL Players Association, the Packers have decided to give their four days off following the first game after the bye.

It makes sense; there are fewer total days between the Packers’ Week 10 game and their Week 12 game (10) than there are between the Week 12 game and the Week 13 game (11).

The situation flows directly from the decision to play a Wednesday game, on the night before Thanksgiving. It removes the traditional two-week break, cobbling together a pair of mini-byes.

For the players, the break likely will coincide with Thanksgiving weekend, possibly giving them Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday off.

The Rams, in contrast, will surely be taking their four-day break before the Week 12 Wednesday night game. They play their Week 13 game against the Chiefs only eight days later, on the following Thursday night.

sports.title: NFL flexes Raiders-Browns to Sunday night in Week 12

sports.title: Brian Flores: Vikings plan to rotate players in order to deal with altitude in Mexico City
sports.summary: The 49ers are spending the week in Colorado in order to acclimate to the altitude at which their Week 11 game in Mexico City will be played.
sports.body:
But the Vikings have a plan for ensuring that their players are ready for the conditions.

“It’s a tough place to play,” Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores told reporters on Tuesday regarding the game in Mexico. “I think it’s certainly taxing, you know, I think you’re — I think as a staff, we’re already talking about, ‘Hey, we’re gonna have to rotate these guys and get, you know, everybody’s gonna have to be ready to play.’ And so, yeah, I mean, it’s certainly something that we’re going to have to deal with.

“But there’s always, you know, elements that we’re dealing with, whether it’s cold or rain or things like that. Obviously, we’re indoors, so we don’t deal with much of that. But that’s the environment we’re gonna be in. I think we prepare them to play in that environment, but I’m not gonna be silly and say, ‘Hey, everybody, hey, you’ve got to go in there for 12 straight plays.’ I mean, we’re not doing that.

“So we’ll have rotations, we’ll have a plan in place. Inevitably, we’re gonna have to fight through some of that. It’s not gonna be your average game where, you know, altitude, you just have — you literally have less oxygen. So we’ve got to do a great job as a staff of making sure — watching guys, and making sure we got guys in and out, you know, as much as we can.”

His broader message to the defense is clear: “We’re gonna need everybody.”

Regardless of the plan to rotate players, the question becomes whether the 49ers will be able to rely more heavily on their best players because they’re properly acclimated to the thinner air. The Vikings are choosing a different strategy, and it’s going to create an obvious apples to apples comparison between the approaches that the two teams have taken — especially if the 49ers players seem to be fresh and the Vikings players seem to be gassed.

sports.title: CB Nazeeh Johnson visited the Steelers Tuesday

According to multiple reports, Johnson visited with the Steelers on Tuesday.

sports.title: Jim Leonhard has embraced aggressiveness in Buffalo Bills defensive scheme since bye week
sports.summary: Yes, the Buffalo Bills have gone from a gauntlet of high-level quarterbacks to start to the season to a consecutive collection of backups, and that drastic shift in competition has coincided with a drastic shift in defensive philosophy from Jim Leonhard. In the first six games of the 2026 season, wh
sports.body: Yes, the Buffalo Bills have gone from a gauntlet of high-level quarterbacks to start to the season to a consecutive collection of backups, and that drastic shift in competition has coincided with a drastic shift in defensive philosophy from Jim Leonhard. In the first six games of the 2026 season, when Buffalo’s defense was a liability, the Bills played man coverage 16.4% of the time, per Fantasy Points Data. That was the 24th-highest man-coverage rate in the NFL. Also in those first six outings, Buffalo’s blitz rate was 27.9%, the 20th-highest blitz rate in football. Then the bye week happened. Since then, the Bills’ man-coverage rate jumped to 25.7%. In that three-game sample, that’s the 13th-highest in the league. Buffalo’s blitz rate has been 33.6% combined in Weeks 8, 9, and 10, the 13th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. (Can’t forget too — there was plenty of garbage time in all three contests, where the Bills, like any team, were prompted to sit back in soft zone to keep everything in front of them.) The new man-coverage and blitz rates don’t represent massive, 180-degree changes in philosophy. And we likely won’t be able to fully discern how much Leonhard’s man-coverage and blitzing movement post-bye has actually made the Bills defense better until Thanksgiving night against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. But one thing is for sure — Leonhard’s defense has recently started to look like what we expected Leonhard’s defense to look like all along.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills not only beat the New York Jets, but they did so in pretty convincing fashion. There’s just one problem though. Three weeks ago, MVP Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson exited the contest after one play. This past week, they got a heavy dose of former Clemson quarterback and rookie Cade Klubnik when New York Jets starter Geno Smith was in and out of the game. The results over these past three weeks (henceforth referred to as “the improvement period”) have been excellent for the Bills defense. The obvious caveat to any discussion here is that the results should be excellent due to the level of play challenging the Buffalo defense, but strong play against backup quarterbacks is certainly preferable to poor play against backup quarterbacks. Over this improvement period, the Bills have posted negative EPA per play each week (negative is good for defensive EPA) after only posting a negative EPA per play one time prior (week three against the hapless-thus-far-in-2026 Los Angeles Chargers offense). They also posted sub-45% success rates each week after only achieving that once before in 2026 (again, against the Chargers). It’s unquestionably the best stretch of defense the Bills have delivered so far during the regular season, and it comes not just against backup quarterbacks, but also in the three weeks immediately following the Buffalo bye week in Week 7. They’ve achieved these results through very different means. Against the Ravens, the Bills employed a blitz-heavy approach (61.3%, a season-high) with a large amount of man coverage (54.8%, also a season-high). The veteran wideout was waived by the Eagles over the weekend and has now cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent. Sure, the Bills are probably close to seeing Tyrell Shavers return to the field, which will make for a somewhat crowded receiver room. Back in 2023, Sal Maiorana of the Rochester Democrat & Chronicle selected Brown as a potential trade target for the Bills at the deadline. Brown was not traded then and ended the season with 51 catches for 574 yards with four scores on 69% of Arizona’s offensive snaps. Then, after a season with the Chiefs in 2024, the Buffalo’s supposed interest in Brown was documented in a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler in early February 2025: > “Mahomes advocated for signing Brown last year and will likely do so again. Will another star quarterback -- like Josh Allen -- be next? If the Bills do sign Brown, it’d hardly be the first time they added a receiver after a stint as a complementary piece in Kansas City (see: Marquez-Valdes Scantling and Mecole Hardman). sports.body: We have seven more games left in the Aaron Glenn era for the New York Jets. I will not remember this time period fondly whatsoever, but don’t worry, because there is a light at the end of the tunnel. ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast that he could potentially see the team making an aggressive move to trade for their next head coach. Cimini said, “The name I would watch for is KOC, Kevin O’Connell. I was just talking to a couple of people in the league today, and they said they could see [Darren] Mougey giving up a high draft pick for Kevin O’Connell. They went to college together; they have maintained a relationship. If something falls apart there in Minnesota, if they collapse down the stretch, or if they decide that they want to elevate [Brian] Flores instead of losing him to another team, maybe they make that move.” Cimini revealed that, “I was told Mougey even in meetings like offseason and preseason has spoken, internal meetings with the Jets has spoken highly of O’Connell has mentioned him in meetings and so I wouldn’t totally dismiss that. I mean, he would come in, they would get along great, they have a history, he is an offensive-minded coach with coaching experience. Now, he has made a couple of questionable quarterback decisions in Minnesota. I don’t know how much of that is him or the GM or the previous GM, but I think it’s a name to watch for; let me put that out there.” Oh baby! Spicy! Sexy! Interesting! Now I’m sure there will be a huge debate in the comment section about whether this is too crazy or even worth it. Before you run to the comments, I would just like to provide some statistical data about KOC. The Jets, in their team history, have only ever won 12 games in a regular season once (1998). O’Connell is in his fifth season as a head coach in the NFL. He has already surpassed that number twice with a 14-win season (2024) and a 13-win season (2022). Who knows if he will add a third such year to his resume; the Vikings are currently 7-2. KOC is awesome, and if the Jets can find a way, they should absolutely explore it. --- J-E-T-S! sports.body: The Buffalo Bills are leading the NFL in points per game at 31.9, and they’re 8-1 for the first time since 1991, but there’s always room for improvement. And I think said improvement can occur in Buffalo’s pass game if slot receiver Khalil Shakir becomes a focal point. I won’t fault you for questioning why I’m writing this now after Shakir had two catches for 29 yards — along with three “runs” for 26 yards — in the win over the Jets in Week 10. There are a few reasons — it’s a follow from one of my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory in MetLie Stadium, Amon-Ra St. Brown went off for the Lions against the Patriots in Germany, and Parker Washington had the most receiving yards in a game (152) for the Jaguars since 2019. Oh, and now is the ideal time to start incorporating Shakir into a more prominent role, right before the Bills have this five-game stretch during the holiday season — vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers, vs. Bears, and at Broncos. Let’s start general, with a question — who has been the Bills most reliable receiver for going on four seasons now? Shakir. Even in 2023, his second season as a professional, on a team with Stefon Diggs, Shakir’s yards-per-route run (1.79) rivaled Diggs’ (1.89). His drop rate was drastically lower than Diggs’ 2.0% vs. 6.4%, and he averaged 7.0 yards after contact per reception to Diggs’ 3.9. All those figures are counting the playoffs too. Even if you believed Diggs was more reliable in 2023, from 2024 to the present day, we can all agree the answer to my original question is Shakir, right? sports.body: Josh Allen has as many rushing touchdowns as Eric Dickerson. Yes, we’re comparing a quarterback to the guy who ran for 2,105 yards in one season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2122058091134881834?a=hfBRzB3qb8hT6ZX9EDw&s=20] Allen scored his 90th career rushing touchdown during Buffalo’s Week 10 game against the New York Jets, tying Dickerson and fellow Hall of Famer Curtis Martin for 14th on the NFL’s all-time list. He entered the game with 88. Number 89 came on a one yard run in the first quarter. Number 90 was a two-yard run on the Bills’ first possession of the third quarter. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2122034725476766076?a=C37X0KjNpeEIGge-adI&s=20] [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2122057732488376770?a=x6C71tZcVsvn-l8ycns&s=20] Dickerson and Martin weren’t running backs who had a few good seasons. Dickerson led the NFL in rushing four times, and nobody has topped his single-season yardage record in more than 40 years. Martin opened his career with 10 straight 1,000-yard seasons, including seven with the New York Jets. Bills fans had plenty of opportunities to get tired of watching him, but now they can celebrate one of their own making what he did look average. Both finished with 90 rushing touchdowns. Allen has matched them in his ninth season while also being responsible for, you know, throwing the football. The quarterback record is already his. It has been for a while. Now Allen has reached the point where we’re comparing his touchdown total to some of the best running backs to ever play, and he could pass a few more before this season is over. One more rushing touchdown would tie Jerome Bettis and Franco Harris for 12th at 91. Barry Sanders is next at 99, followed by Marshall Faulk and Shaun Alexander at 100. Allen would need 10 more to join that pair in ninth place, which is asking a lot. But we’re talking about a quarterback with a chance to finish the season in the NFL’s top 10 for career rushing touchdowns. We can keep asking him to slide, but we shouldn’t expect that he will. Apparently, he has a few more people to catch first.

sports.body: > “I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs.” That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the television series, The Office. Michael Scott didn’t end up losing his job as branch manager of Dunder-Mifflin in the end. Nevertheless, the review remains relatable. Sometimes people can improve their job performance, but other times you reach a realization that they just aren’t capable of doing it. We are past that stage with Aaron Glenn. We can point to any number of dubious marks of his resume as Jets head coach. He is now 5-22, sporting a worse winning percentage as an NFL head coach than Hue Jackson. Glenn now has more than twice as many double digit point losses than he has wins. The latest defeat was the ugly 31-12 blowout at the hands of the Buffalo Bills in Week 10. There isn’t much drama left surrounding Glenn. Barring an unexpected late season surge, he will not retain his job as Jets head coach for a third year. Even if there is a late season winning streak, it still might not be enough. NFL teams don’t reassign their coach to a different department. Coaching contracts aren’t written that way, and practical considerations make the sort of demotion recommended for Scott unviable. Glenn will be let go. He will make enough money to leave football if he so chooses. If he decides to continue his coaching career, he will be an in demand candidates for teams seeking a new defensive coordinator. In the meantime, we will have to endure seven more games. That will be no easy task. I am sure the Jets will invent new ways to lose along the way.
